reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement. Atezolizumab serum concentrations achieved expected levels, confirming PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor reached its target. The combination includes cobimetinib (MEK inhibitor) and vemurafenib (BRAF inhibitor) which are established targeted therapies with known target engagement profiles. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: While specific pathway biomarkers aren't detailed, the combination rationale of checkpoint blockade plus MAPK pathway inhibition is mechanistically sound. Anti-drug antibodies developed in 13.3% of patients, indicating immune system recognition of atezolizumab. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint was met with statistical significance. PFS improved from 10.6 months (control) to 15.1 months (triple combination), HR 0.79, p=0.0224. OS also showed numerical improvement (25.8 vs 39.0 months) though not statistically significant (p=0.1191). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Trial enrolled BRAF V600 mutation-positive patients, the appropriate biomarker-selected population for this combination. No subgroup analyses reported, but the overall population was mechanistically appropriate. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Well-designed randomized controlled trial with adequate duration (369 weeks). Safety profile showed increased AEs in combination arm (100% vs 99.6% any AE, 50.9% vs 43.0% SAEs) but no dose-limiting toxicity that prevented efficacy assessment.

failure_modes.evidence: OS endpoint showed numerical improvement but missed statistical significance (p=0.1191), suggesting longer follow-up might be needed for this endpoint
